name: Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration
dates: Eleven days ending the Saturday before Labor Day
unique: The world championship of the Tennessee Walking Horse, eleven days and nights of classes in the big arena where the breed's high stepping running walk is judged, with a trade fair, a barn row you can walk and a grand entry every night.
buzz: The show is spectacle even for people who know nothing about horses, and the barns are where the owners and trainers talk. The breed's show history includes a federal abuse scandal, and the industry is still arguing about it, which the program and the exhibitors will discuss if asked.

name: Bell Buckle RC Cola and MoonPie Festival
customer: Families, day trippers from Nashville, food crowds
unique: A one day festival celebrating the southern snack of an RC Cola and a MoonPie, with a MoonPie toss, a ten mile run, clogging on the main street and a world record attempt for the largest MoonPie, in a town of six hundred people.
buzz: It is hot, crowded and completely sincere, and people come back every year. The MoonPie eating contest and the RC chug are the events everyone photographs.

name: Bell Buckle Historic District
dates: Year round, shops closed some weekdays
unique: A railroad town of clapboard storefronts and Victorian houses on the National Register, with a cafe that has been serving pie for decades, antique shops and a Webb School campus on the hill above.
buzz: It is a twenty minute walk and a two hour browse, and the pie is the reason people come back. Weekends are busy and the town is small enough to feel borrowed for the day.

name: Shelbyville Court Square
unique: A courthouse square in the walking horse capital, ringed by shops and saddlers, with the county's memorials and a monument to the breed on the lawn.
buzz: During the Celebration the square is full of out of state trucks and horse trailers. The rest of the year it is a quiet county seat with good lunch counters.

name: Short Mountain Distillery
dates: Weekends, tours at one and three
customer: Whiskey drinkers, groups, live music fans
unique: A farm distillery at the foot of Short Mountain making moonshine and whiskey from corn grown on the property, with a stone still house, a tasting room in a barn and weekend tours that start with the grain and end with the jar.
buzz: The tour is short and the tasting is generous, and the live music on the porch is the reason people stay. Groups book ahead and the drive out is a back road through Cannon County.

name: Arts Center of Cannon County
unique: A nonprofit arts center with a playhouse, galleries and a concert hall under one roof, running a full season of musicals and plays with local casts in a county of fourteen thousand people.
buzz: The productions are ambitious for the size of the town and the tickets are cheap. People drive from Murfreesboro for the bigger shows.

name: Woodbury Court Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse on a rise above the shops, in a county named for a governor and known for moonshine before it was legal.
buzz: Short and steep and easy to walk. The square is where you eat before the distillery tour.

name: Brownsport Furnace
unique: The stone stack and ruins of a charcoal fired iron furnace that smelted Tennessee brown ore before the Civil War, in a county park with trails, picnic shelters and the old ore pits still visible in the woods.
buzz: The stack is bigger than people expect and the interpretive signs explain the slave and hired labor that ran it. It is free, quiet and used by local trail riders.

name: Carroll Cabin Barrens State Natural Area
company: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
unique: Two hundred fifty acres of limestone glades and barrens on the hills above the Tennessee River, with little bluestem grass, stunted red cedars and wildflowers that grow in thin soil over Silurian rock.
buzz: Botanists come for the glade plants and most other people have never heard of it. The trail is short and the ground is fragile, so stay on it.

name: Decaturville Court Square
unique: A small square with a 1920s courthouse, a monument and the storefronts of a county seat that sits inland from the river it depends on, a few minutes from the Tennessee.
buzz: Very quiet, with the river five miles east and one cafe on the square. People stop on the way to the boat ramp.

name: Tims Ford State Park
unique: Three thousand acres around a TVA lake on the Elk River with a golf course, campgrounds, cabins, a marina and a shoreline of coves where the water is deep and the bass fishing is serious.
buzz: The lake is the reason and the golf course is the surprise. Anglers fish the grass for largemouth and the river below the dam for trout in winter.

name: Sewanee Natural Bridge
company: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
unique: A twenty five foot high sandstone arch with a fifty foot span on the Cumberland Plateau, with a short trail down under the span and a spring that seeps along the rock in wet weather.
buzz: It is a five minute walk from the parking area and children climb under it. People pair it with the university and the trailheads at Fiery Gizzard.

name: University of the South at Sewanee
unique: A Episcopal liberal arts college on a plateau bought from the Sewanee Mining Company, with a Gothic stone campus of Tennessee limestone, an All Saints' Chapel with a set of bells and a cemetery with bishops in it, all on a ridge above the valley.
buzz: The campus is open to walkers and the stone work in late afternoon light is the reason people detour. The chapel is the one building everybody goes into.

name: Winchester Court Square
unique: A square with a 1930s courthouse in the middle of town, surrounded by brick storefronts and a farmers market, in the seat of a county that has been a crossroads since the federal road went through.
buzz: The square is a real one, with a hardware store and lunch counters. People stop before Tims Ford and end up walking it twice.

name: Trousdale County Museum and Train Depot
company: Trousdale County and the Chamber of Commerce
unique: A restored 1800s depot that now holds the county museum and the chamber, with railroad artifacts, tobacco warehouse photographs and the story of a county flooded repeatedly by the Cumberland.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and the volunteers know the flood history. Tennessee's smallest county in land area packs a lot into one room.

name: Hartsville Battlefield
unique: The ground where on December 7, 1862 John Hunt Morgan's cavalry surrounded and captured most of a Union brigade in a fight that lasted about two hours, with markers and a small preserved area near town.
buzz: Barely developed and easy to miss, which is why the people who find it tend to be reading their way through the Stones River campaign. The story is better than the ground.

name: Hartsville Historic Downtown
unique: A downtown that has been rebuilt after Cumberland River floods more than once, with a courthouse, storefronts and the Avery Trace running through the county on its way from Knoxville to Nashville.
buzz: Small and plain and honest about the water. People come for the depot and stay to walk two blocks.

name: Big Ridge State Park
unique: Thirty six hundred acres of ridge and hollow above Norris Lake built by the CCC and TVA in the 1930s, with log cabins, a swimming beach on Big Ridge Lake and trails past the old Norton Creek cemetery and mill site.
buzz: The cabins and the beach are booked all summer and the trails are quiet the rest of the year. People who grew up camping here bring their grandchildren.

name: Norris Lake
dates: Year round, best May to October
unique: A TVA reservoir in the Clinch and Powell river valleys with more than eight hundred miles of shoreline, clear deep water, houseboat rentals and drowned towns under the surface.
buzz: Boaters call it the cleanest lake in east Tennessee and the coves are quiet even in July. Anglers fish for bass and stripers below the dam.

name: Maynardville Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1960s courthouse and a ring of shops in the seat of a county created in 1850 out of pieces of five others, named for a landowner who gave the land for the town.
buzz: A few blocks and a couple of stores, five minutes from the lake. Most visitors are buying ice and bait.

name: Van Buren County Historical and Heritage Museum
company: Van Buren County Historical and Heritage Museum
unique: A county collection in Spencer covering the farms, mills and schools of a plateau county that made its money from timber and its reputation from a state park and a trial that moved the county seat.
buzz: Volunteers open it and are happy to explain the county's feud over the courthouse. It is small and free and the air conditioning is welcome after the gorge.

name: Spencer Courthouse Square
unique: A tiny square with a 1900s courthouse, a monument and the storefronts of a town of a thousand people that serves as the base for Fall Creek Falls and the plateau's back roads.
buzz: Two blocks and one store. Everybody passing through on the way to the falls drives by it and almost nobody stops.
